text:
Maya Rivera: Quick Q — returning from intermittent FMLA next week and noticed I missed 4 pay periods of 401(k) deferrals earlier this year during unpaid leave. Can I make up the pre-tax deferrals after I return? Also, I had HSA payroll contributions stopped; how do I get back on and is there any way to hit the annual HSA max if I miss months?

Liam O'Connor: Welcome back in advance! Short answer: pre-tax 401(k) deferrals must be taken via payroll. You can increase your deferral % when you return to try to "catch up" within IRS limits, but you can't retroactively force payroll to withhold from past paychecks.

Maya Rivera: Got it. Is there a process for the company to do a manual correction or deposit to my 401(k)? I heard some companies can do post-payroll corrections.

Priya Singh: Hi Maya — manual corrections are rare and require plan admin approval + rationale (e.g., payroll error). For unpaid leave where no earnings exist, plan sponsors typically don't allow retroactive employee pre-tax contributions to be credited to missed pay periods. We can submit a request to benefits@redwood.com if you'd like them to confirm with Fidelity.

FidelityBot: System notice: "Recordkeeper rules: employee pre-tax deferrals must originate from employer payroll. After-tax or rollover contributions may be accepted subject to plan terms. Contact planadmin@fidelity.com for exceptions."

Maya Rivera: OK. Suppose I bump my deferral from 5% to 20% when I return to try to approximate what I missed — any pitfalls? Limits?

Liam O'Connor: Make sure you stay under the 2026 employee elective deferral limit (check current IRS limit). Also be mindful of paycheck withholding and take-home pay. Payroll can apply the new percentage starting the first eligible pay after your return. If you want automated help, set it in the Benefits Portal and cc payroll@redwood.com.

Priya Singh: For employer match: matches are calculated on contributions withheld each pay. Missing pay periods means no match for those periods, unless plan admin approves an adjustment, which is unusual. If hitting match vesting is a concern, share your hire date and I can confirm vesting status.

Maya Rivera: Hire date 2020-04-02. Would appreciate vesting check.

Priya Singh: Noted — I will check vesting and follow up.

Maya Rivera: About HSA — I had been contributing $150/pay and stopped during leave. If I increase to $300/pay when I return, can I still reach the family/yearly max? Is midyear election changes allowed?

FidelityBot: HSA rules: you can change HSA payroll contributions midyear if your plan permits midyear election changes. The HSA annual contribution limit is calendar-year based; you can contribute up to the limit as long as you don't exceed it across all sources. If you enroll in HSA-eligible coverage midyear, different rules (pro-rata testing) may apply.

Priya Singh: Redwood allows HSA deferral changes via Benefits Portal anytime for active pay. If you want to frontload, increase payroll amount once you return. Note: if you use a pre-tax payroll HSA and are under HDHP for the whole year, no pro-rata. If you only have HDHP part-year, ask benefits@redwood.com — there are testing rules.

Liam O'Connor: Another practical tip: if you need to maximize HSA quickly, you can also make an after-tax contribution to your HSA account directly and then do a tax-deductible adjustment on your tax return (or trustee-to-trustee transfers) — but check with a tax advisor.

Maya Rivera: Thanks — please proceed with vesting check. Also please submit a plan admin question about whether any manual match correction is possible (I know it's unlikely but want it documented).

Priya Singh: Will do. Submitting to plan admin now and will reply here when they confirm.

hr-bot: Policy note (automated): "401(k) employee deferrals must be remitted via payroll withholding. Employer matching contributions are based on actual payroll contributions. HSA payroll deferrals are elective and can be adjusted on return to active pay. Exceptions require plan admin approval and documentation."

Priya Singh: Update (plan admin reply): Manual retroactive employee pre-tax deferrals for unpaid leave are not permitted under current plan terms. They can accept after-tax rollovers/loans subject to limits. Employer match cannot be credited for periods with no contributions. Vesting: continuous service counts for your sabbatical/intermittent FMLA — no vesting interruption. I emailed the formal response to you, Maya.

Maya Rivera: Thanks everyone — that clarifies things. I will set a higher deferral upon return, and consider front-loading HSA as suggested. Appreciate the quick responses. :pray:
